title: Masked Gaze
coreRelationships: The sharp, detailed eyes contrast strongly with the soft, blurred, and obscured figure.
The vertical strips of masking tape create a repetitive pattern that acts as a visual barrier.
The light, translucent quality of the tape overlays the darker, underlying photographic image.
The central placement of the eyes draws immediate attention, despite the surrounding obstruction.
reuseFormula: Generate a portrait of a person, then apply a textured, translucent, vertical stripe overlay that obscures most of the face and body, leaving only a horizontal strip containing the eyes clearly visible. Maintain a desaturated color palette.
typographyText: none · none · none · none · none · Generate a monochromatic or sepia-toned photographic image of a female figure, facing forward, with a neutral expression. Ensure the figure fills most of the frame vertically and is centrally aligned. The lighting should be soft and even, avoiding harsh shadows. The background should be plain and light. The eyes should be clearly visible and have dark, defined makeup. Then, apply a filter or overlay that simulates vertical strips of translucent, slightly aged masking tape covering most of the image, leaving only a horizontal strip across the eyes relatively clear. The tape strips should have subtle texture and varying opacity, with some edges appearing torn or slightly crumpled. · No text overlay is present in the original image. If text is to be added, it should be done thoughtfully to avoid competing with the strong visual focus on the eyes and the textured tape. Consider a subtle, minimalist approach, perhaps in a desaturated tone that blends with the overall palette. · Are the eyes the clearest and most detailed element? · Is the figure predominantly obscured by vertical strips? · Does the obscuring material resemble aged, textured masking tape? · Is the overall color scheme desaturated or monochromatic? · Is there a strong contrast between the eyes and the surrounding obscured areas? · high
